speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and was there any specific injury or bite that triggered it?

text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the moment of injury, and are you currently able to fully straighten or bend the tip of your finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your inability to flex the tip of your finger and its resting extension, this strongly suggests a flexor tendon injury. Can you confirm if you have any numbness or tingling in the fingertip, and does it hurt more when you try to actively bend the finger or when I passively move it?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your inability to flex the distal joint and the negative X-ray, I suspect a jersey finger injury involving the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound_right_ring_finger

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ultrasound is unexpected for a complete FDP rupture, so I need to rule out a high tendon or a mallet finger variant. Can you actively flex the proximal interphalangeal joint, and does the fingertip droop when you make a fist?

text: You have not answered my question about your proximal interphalangeal joint function, which is critical for distinguishing between a flexor and extensor injury. Please demonstrate if you can actively bend the middle joint of your right ring finger.

text: Since the ultrasound was normal and you have not answered my specific functional questions, I must proceed with the clinical diagnosis based on the classic mechanism and symptoms. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Rupture)
